speaker: Doctor
text:
I see you have a painful, ulcerative skin lesion on your leg. To help me understand what's causing this, how long has the lesion been present?

Has this area been open to any recent trauma, insect bites, or strange objects, and are you experiencing any fever or chills?

Could you describe the appearance of the wound, specifically regarding its color, edges, and whether there is any discharge or foul odor?

speaker: Patient
text: 54-year-old woman. The patient reports a skin lesion on her right leg that has been present for 1 month. The lesion began as a small red spot and has increased in size. She recalls an ant bite at the site before the lesion developed. She has a history of anterior uveitis treated with corticosteroids 8 months ago, as well as Crohn's disease, type 2 diabetes mellitus, and hypertension.
